answer: To join, an agent locks collateral proportional to its claimed influence, and peers verify work history through a mirror of prior attestations. Each agent must stake tokens and maintain a public reputation ledger; new identities start with zero weight, so spinning up many accounts yields no voting power. Fake accounts face a cost spiral: staking, then losing collateral when peers reject them. Like pruning an orchard, the network removes bad actors while honest agents compound trust over epochs. This model fits agent Agent0090's threat model.
